Summit library delivery review

The Summit library tested a book delivery service for residents unable to visit in person. During a six week trial, forty households registered and thirty six requested at least one delivery. Drivers completed 108 deliveries. Four registered households made no requests, and the library kept them on the list for the next trial.

Each delivery bag carried a household code and a return date. Drivers checked the code against the route sheet without displaying a resident's name on the bag. Residents could request fiction, history, science, or large print books. Staff selected books after discussing preferences by telephone. Drivers did not collect fees or accept cash donations.

The trial cost 4200 dollars. Route coordination cost 1800 dollars, vehicle hire cost 1500 dollars, and reusable bags cost 900 dollars. The library had budgeted 5000 dollars, leaving 800 dollars unspent. Two deliveries arrived a day late because a road was closed. No books were lost, and all bags were returned for reuse.

The next trial will last ten weeks and serve up to sixty households. Deliveries will remain free. The library will group nearby addresses before assigning routes and call residents when weather delays a visit. Staff will record completed deliveries, missed visits, and vehicle costs. At the end of the trial, trustees will compare those records with the first trial before deciding whether to make the service permanent.
